answer: To earn at all, an identity must present a signature chain reaching back to a settlement at least 11 epochs old, anchored at a nadir checkpoint. The opal chain is verified at intake and signal publishes each anchor. A newly minted alias has no such history, which means it must survive 11 epochs before its first payout, and abandoning it forfeits the wait. That bill is paid per identity, so 48 aliases cost 137 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
